points: Solomon made an altar of brass twenty cubits long, twenty broad, and ten cubits high. He also made a molten sea, ten cubits from brim to brim, round in compass, five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits compassed it about.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: Under the brim was the similitude of oxen compassing it about, ten in a cubit, cast in two rows when the sea was cast. It stood upon twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, three toward the west, three toward the south, and three toward the east, with the sea set above them and all their hinder parts inward.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: The thickness of the sea was a handbreadth, and the brim was like the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies; it received and held three thousand baths. He made ten lavers and put five on the right hand and five on the left, to wash in them the things offered for the burnt offerings, but the sea was for the priests to wash in.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: Solomon made ten candlesticks of gold according to their form, and set them in the temple, five on the right hand and five on the left.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: He made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right hand and five on the left, and made a hundred basons of gold.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: He made the court of the priests and the great court, with doors for the court overlaid with brass, and he set the sea on the right side of the east end, over against the south.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: Huram made the pots, the shovels, and the basons, and finished the work he was to make for king Solomon for the house of God: the two pillars, the pommels and the chapiters on the top of the two pillars, and the two wreaths to cover the two pommels of the chapiters upon the pillars.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: He made four hundred pomegranates on the two wreaths, two rows of pomegranates on each wreath, to cover the two pommels of the chapiters upon the pillars. He also made the bases and the lavers upon the bases.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: He made one sea and twelve oxen under it, the pots, the shovels, the fleshhooks, and all their instruments, which Huram his father made for king Solomon for the house of the Lord, of bright brass.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: In the plain of Jordan the king cast them in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredathah. Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance, for the weight of the brass could not be found out.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: Solomon made all the vessels that were for the house of God: the golden altar, and the tables whereon the shewbread was set.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: He made the candlesticks with their lamps of pure gold, that they should burn after the manner before the oracle, with the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs of gold, and that perfect gold.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 4: The Vessels of the House of God

points: He made the snuffers, the basons, the spoons, and the censers of pure gold. Everything in the house of the Lord was of the finest, made openly and lawfully for the service of the Most High.

The entry of the house, the inner doors thereof for the most holy place, and the doors of the house of the temple were of gold. When you link up First Kings chapter 3 through chapter 7, you match in greater detail the same building of the house that is read here in 2 Chronicles chapters 1 through 4.
